g0.placementConjunctNote: The directions state 'von den Wurzeln bis in die Spitzen' — explicit ROOT application, which contradicts P5's canonical 'Längen und Spitzen, Ansatz aussparen'. Under R8's mask delta this is a protocol deviation that fires the root/scalp application review trigger; it does not silently change R8 and does not create a scalp property. Eligibility was not refused: the stated placement INCLUDES lengths and ends, and the charter names this product as included by identity. See AP-11-ROOTS.

tailMarker.anomalyNote: The earliest tail-class ingredient is a COLOURANT at rank 7 — the only cohort product where the marker is neither a fragrance nor a preservative, and the only one where Parfum is the FINAL entry (rank 30). §3.1's literal anomaly conditions are not met (rank 7 > 3, and Cetearyl Alcohol @2 and Behentrimonium Chloride @4 precede it), so the marker is technically resolved. But a colourant pair at ranks 7–8 in a list whose fragrance sits at 30 is not a plausible ~1% proxy: cosmetic colourants are typically used far below 1%, and this ordering is more consistent with a house listing convention or a retailer transcription artefact than with descending weight. I therefore fire `tail_marker_anomaly` by reviewer judgment and cap every affected field at moderate confidence, while still applying the marker as written. See AP-11-COLOURANT.

R6a applied: glycolic acid TEMPORARILY PLASTICIZES the fibre (a measured decrease in Young's modulus). It does not seal, coat, close the cuticle, laminate, or produce lasting change, and it contributes nothing to this field.
counterSignals: The pack claims 'versiegelt die Haaroberfläche mit intensivem, langanhaltendem Glanz' and the directions say 'brillant zu versiegeln'. Both use wording that R6a and §9.5.4 place on an absolute banned list. They are quoted here strictly as claim context; no part of this record adopts sealing, lasting, or lamination language.

primaryFocus.evidenceScope: Formula-first §9.5.2 hierarchy over above-tail ranks 1–6; §9.5.4 shine threshold with its claim-gated third criterion.
primaryFocus.rationale: All three §9.5.4 criteria are met. The formula shape is the one §9.5.4 criterion 1 describes as distinguishing a gloss product from a rich nourishing mask — an alignment-oriented amino silicone above the tail with a comparatively low lipid load, and here the lipid load above the tail is literally zero. The claim leg is satisfied by unambiguous exact-product Gloss/Laminierung/Glanz positioning, used as corroboration only. E2 ceiling: temporary optical/surface emphasis and comparative shine POTENTIAL — never sealing, never lasting.
evidenceSignals: AMODIMETHICONE (rank 6) — alignment-oriented R2 silicone above the tail
zero R4b heavy lipids above the tail, and in fact zero lipids of any class above the tail — the comparatively low lipid load criterion 1 requires
COCOS NUCIFERA OIL (rank 9) — the formula's only heavy lipid candidate, BELOW the marker, so criterion 1's lipid condition is satisfied on the credited segment
POLYQUATERNIUM-37 (rank 17) and HYDROXYPROPYL GUAR (rank 11) — cationic polymers, both in the tail; the optical route rests on the silicone alone
GLYCOLIC ACID (rank 29) — R6a acid-gloss context: supporting context, never sufficient, and here it earns nothing at its rank
claims: '19% Gloss-Complex mit Glykolsäure', 'erstes Haar-Laminierungs-Produkt von L'Oréal Paris für zuhause', 'für stumpfes, poröses Haar'; product name 'Glycolic Gloss, 5-Minuten Haar-Laminierung'
primaryFocus.derivation: Step 1 baseline exclusion applied. Step 2: one M1 base observation plus one M3 optical observation. Step 3: `repair` blocked (no R5, no bond, and R6a can never set repair); `curl_support` blocked (single cationic, no above-tail polymer); `color_care` blocked (no colour-protection candidate and no colour-protection positioning — the CI entries are the product's own dye load, and colour-DEPOSITING masks are excluded at G0 in any case); `lightness` blocked (weight `moderate`, not `low`). Step 4 `moisture` blocked (one above-tail humectant against a required three). Step 5 `shine`: all three criteria evaluated and met.
thresholdReasoning: Criterion 1 CLEARS: a distinct optical emphasis architecture — an alignment-oriented R2 silicone above the tail — with a comparatively low lipid load and no R4b heavy lipid above the tail. This directly answers §18 open question 6, which asked whether the low-lipid-load criterion would exclude products the charter explicitly wants classified as shine-focused. For this product it does not: the credited segment is lipid-free, so the criterion is met comfortably rather than narrowly.

Criterion 2 CLEARS: the optical route is not merely a smoothing film already counted. No smoothing focus was awarded, and the architecture is not the ordinary M1 deposition — it is a lipid-free, single-silicone, alignment-oriented shape. §9.5.4's fallback instruction ('if the same M1/M3 deposition is the sole basis, select smoothing') would apply to a formula whose optical claim rested on nothing but its conditioning base; this formula's base is unusually thin and the silicone is the distinct addition.

Criterion 3 CLEARS on claim corroboration — the one legitimately claim-gated leg in this record, and the only place in the entire cohort where unblinding changed a value. Gloss, Glaze, Laminierung and Glanz positioning are all present in the exact-product name and claims. Corroboration only: it could not have created the route, and criteria 1 and 2 were established blind.
`smoothing` was the blind-lane value and lost to `shine` only on criterion 3. Recorded as a blind-to-final change with its reason.
`general` does not apply: a candidate cleared at step 5.
There is NO lamination property and no `lamination` focus value. Gloss identity is carried entirely by `shine`, per charter F4, D2 and evidence §7.
counterSignals: The `tail_marker_anomaly` matters more here than anywhere else: if the marker were taken at Phenoxyethanol @13 instead of the colourant @7, Cocos Nucifera Oil @9 and Hydroxypropyl Guar @11 would come above the tail. The coconut oil is an R4b heavy lipid, which would defeat criterion 1's low-lipid-load condition and collapse `shine` to `smoothing` or `general`. This is the single most marker-sensitive focus call in the cohort.
The exact-product claim '19% Gloss-Complex' is an E0 marketing figure and is not a concentration fact; no percentage was inferred from it.

Glycolic acid's skin-exfoliation evidence is not imported, and its position (rank 29, second from last) is the lexicon's own standing reminder that acid-led positioning and acid-led architecture are unrelated.
limitations: Banned wording, absolute (evidence §7, §9.5.4, R6a): this record never says seals, versiegelt, closes the cuticle, laminates, lasting, permanent, or builds a protective layer that stays — notwithstanding that the product's own pack and directions use two of those words. Permitted and used: temporary optical/surface emphasis, comparative shine potential.

The optical mechanism behind gloss (surface smoothing raising specular reflection) is not separable from ordinary smoothing-film shine; `shine` here is a positioning-corroborated architectural reading, not a measured optical result. Goniophotometry or blinded visual assessment would be required for E3.

focusCareVerdict.note: The chosen focus is not a repair/moisture decision — it is an optical one, so §9.5.1's repair/moisture verdict set does not apply. Recorded for completeness: on the repair/moisture axis the formula would read `nonspecific` (no protein, one humectant, generic conditioning). claim_role is `corroborating` and points specifically at §9.5.4 criterion 3, the one claim-gated leg in this record. blindToFinalChanges.reason: THE ONLY VALUE CHANGE PRODUCED BY UNBLINDING ANYWHERE IN THIS COHORT. Blind, the formula cleared §9.5.4 criteria 1 and 2 — an alignment-oriented amino silicone at rank 6 with zero lipid load above the tail — but criterion 3 requires exact-product Gloss/Glaze/Laminierung/Glanz positioning, which is by construction unavailable in a blind packet. The hierarchy therefore fell through to step 6 and returned `smoothing`. On unblinding, criterion 3 was satisfied unambiguously by the product name and claims, and `shine` was selected at step 5. This is §11 step 4's first permitted channel working exactly as designed, and it is the reason the shine focus is claim-gated in the first place.
Consequential change following the primaryFocus change, via D2's deterministic benefits derivation.

No dual_supported tie, no bond claim, no lightness positioning to trigger the §9.2 conflict fallback, and no colour-protection positioning. In particular the gloss claim did NOT touch conditioning_level, care_direction, repair_support_level, or the moisture guard — §11 step 4 forbids all four.

adjudicationPoints.title: A colourant as tail marker is reproducible but not plausible, and it decides this product's headline
adjudicationPoints.body: §3.1 lists 'any CI 1xxxx / CI 7xxxx' as a tail class. In this formula the colourant pair sits at ranks 7 and 8 while Parfum is the final entry at rank 30, so the mechanical marker is the colourant and the credited segment is six entries. Cosmetic colourants are typically used at a small fraction of 1%, far below the ~0.2–1% band the lexicon says the fragrance/preservative proxy targets, so a colourant is a systematically EARLIER marker than the rule intends. The consequence here is decisive: at the colourant marker the credited segment is lipid-free and `shine` clears criterion 1; at the next plausible marker (Phenoxyethanol @13) Cocos Nucifera Oil @9 becomes an above-tail R4b heavy lipid, criterion 1 fails, and the primary focus collapses to `smoothing` or `general`. I applied the rule as written and fired `tail_marker_anomaly` by judgment. Candidate fix: remove colourants from the tail-class list and keep them as E1 formula facts only, OR rank colourants below fragrance/preservative in a marker-precedence order rather than taking the strict earliest. Note that the lexicon's own §0.2 definition already differs from the standard's here in the other direction — it includes colourants but omits chelators, which the standard includes.

adjudicationPoints.title: Directions mandating root application on a charter-included product
adjudicationPoints.body: The frozen directions read 'von den Wurzeln bis in die Spitzen brillant zu versiegeln' — root-to-tip application, directly contradicting P5's canonical 'Längen und Spitzen, Ansatz aussparen'. R8's mask delta covers exactly this: it is a protocol deviation that fires the root/scalp review trigger and does not silently change R8 or create a scalp property. But the standard does not say what happens NEXT for a product whose authoritative directions cannot be reconciled with the protocol the engine's stamp requires. Since P5 owns placement and the charter names this product as included, I classified it and flagged the deviation. Nick should decide whether such a product is stampable at all under TPL-MASK, since the protocol's placement slot and the product's own directions disagree.
adjudicationPoints.source: §5 R8 mask delta, §2.5 / P5, charter F4

adjudicationPoints.title: §18 open question 6 answered for this product: the low-lipid-load criterion does NOT exclude it
adjudicationPoints.body: Open question 6 asked whether L'Oréal Glycolic Gloss, Syoss Lamination Intense Glaze and Neqi Gloss Glaze actually clear the three-criterion shine threshold on their real INCIs, or whether the low-lipid-load criterion excludes products the charter explicitly wants classified as shine-focused. For this product, on this formula of record, all three criteria clear and the low-lipid condition is met with room to spare — the credited segment contains no lipid at all. The caveat is AP-11-COLOURANT: the answer is 'yes, comfortably' at the applied marker and 'no' at the next plausible one. The other two gloss products are not in this cohort and remain unanswered.

assumptionNotes: Reviewer policy applied to every record in this lane: §3.1's hard cut determines above-tail membership without exception; the lexicon §0.2 boundary-band caution is applied only as a confidence modifier and never moves a value.

Review triggers fired: `gloss_lamination_claim` (mandatory for any Gloss/Glaze/Laminierung positioning — the shine threshold was verified as independently met on criteria 1 and 2 before the claim was consulted, and the banned wording is absent from every rationale in this record); `tail_marker_anomaly` (fired by reviewer judgment, not by §3.1's literal conditions — see AP-11-COLOURANT); root/scalp application (inherited Conditioner §12 trigger — see AP-11-ROOTS); formula-source conflict (aggregated source, and an order conflict against the lexicon's own worked example for this product family).

Protocol metadata for traceability only, zero classification credit: contact time 5 minutes, also embedded in the product name. Placement per the product's own directions is root-to-tip, which deviates from P5.
Cocamidopropyl Betaine at rank 3 was classified as an amphoteric surfactant and credited toward nothing — neither S1's cationic count nor any care route.

The pack's 'versiegelt' language and the directions' 'brillant zu versiegeln' are quoted as claim context only. Every rationale in this record uses permitted wording: temporary optical/surface emphasis, comparative shine potential. Glycolic acid temporarily plasticizes and does not seal.
